1	"""Simulation study: which factors lower median absolute rent error, and is a heat effect detectable?
2	
3	Synthetic City-of-Sydney-shaped world (all parameters are ASSUMPTIONS, listed in PARAMS / scenario grid).
4	Scoring mimics the task: 1,699 test adverts dated Aug-Sep 2026, training adverts <= 31 Jul 2026,
5	median absolute $ error ranks, share within $100 breaks ties, R^2 reported.
6	
7	Methods (cumulative):
8	  M0  ladder median: suburb x bedrooms x parking -> suburb x bedrooms -> bedrooms (>=10 adverts, last 12 months)  [official example]
9	  M1  own last advert x citywide repeat-rent index; rows without own history use M0
10	  M2  M1 + no-history rows use same-building same-bedroom recent adverts (time-adjusted) when available
11	  M3  M2 + no-history rows use LightGBM on Microburbs-side features (suburb, bed, bath, parking, floor, flats_in_building,
12	      block rent map, building-comps median)
13	  M4  M3 + heat and canopy features
14	Run: python sim/sim_study.py [--quick]
15	"""
16	import argparse
17	import time
18	
19	import lightgbm as lgb
20	import numpy as np
21	import pandas as pd
22	
23	PARAMS = dict(
24	    n_flats=65_777, n_suburbs=33, n_blocks=700, mean_flats_per_building=22,
25	    base_rent=520.0,
26	    sd_suburb=0.10, sd_block=0.07, sd_building=0.10, sd_unit=0.10, sd_advert=0.05,
27	    floor_per_level=0.006, parking=0.08, bath2=0.06,
28	    bed_effect={0: -0.37, 1: 0.0, 2: 0.32, 3: 0.63, 4: 0.92},  # from NSW bond data, CoS flats Aug-Sep 2026 medians
29	    bed_p=[0.10, 0.38, 0.40, 0.10, 0.02],
30	    p_parking=0.55, p_floor_known=0.52, p_ever_advertised=0.76, adverts_per_year=0.30,
31	    corr_heat_affluence=-0.4, corr_heat_canopy=-0.6, block_map_noise=0.03,
32	    n_test=1699,
33	)
34	# calibration target (NSW bond data, CoS flats): within postcode x bedrooms median abs log deviation 0.119
35	MONTHS = pd.period_range("2016-01", "2026-09", freq="M")
36	M_IDX = {p: i for i, p in enumerate(MONTHS)}
37	TRAIN_END = M_IDX[pd.Period("2026-07", "M")]
38	TEST_MONTHS = [M_IDX[pd.Period("2026-08", "M")], M_IDX[pd.Period("2026-09", "M")]]
39	
40	
41	def market_index(n_months, rng):
42	    t = np.arange(n_months) / 12.0
43	    idx = 0.03 * t
44	    covid = (np.arange(n_months) >= M_IDX[pd.Period("2020-04", "M")]) & (np.arange(n_months) <= M_IDX[pd.Period("2021-12", "M")])
45	    idx = idx - 0.12 * covid
46	    rebound = np.clip((np.arange(n_months) - M_IDX[pd.Period("2022-01", "M")]) / 24.0, 0, 1) * 0.08
47	    return idx + rebound + rng.normal(0, 0.005, n_months)
48	
49	
50	def make_world(rng, heat_beta, canopy_beta, p_hist_test):
51	    P = PARAMS
52	    S, B = P["n_suburbs"], P["n_blocks"]
53	    suburb_eff = rng.normal(0, P["sd_suburb"], S)
54	    suburb_growth = rng.normal(0, 0.01, S)
55	    block_suburb = rng.integers(0, S, B)
56	    block_eff = rng.normal(0, P["sd_block"], B)
57	    z_aff = block_eff / P["sd_block"]
58	    r = P["corr_heat_affluence"]
59	    z_heat = r * z_aff + np.sqrt(1 - r * r) * rng.normal(0, 1, B)
60	    rc = P["corr_heat_canopy"]
61	    z_can = rc * z_heat + np.sqrt(1 - rc * rc) * rng.normal(0, 1, B)
62	    env_eff = heat_beta * z_heat + canopy_beta * z_can
63	    # Microburbs block rent map is built from rents, so it already contains the environmental effect
64	    block_map = block_eff + env_eff + rng.normal(0, P["block_map_noise"], B)
65	
66	    # buildings
67	    sizes = []
68	    total = 0
69	    while total < P["n_flats"]:
70	        s = max(1, int(rng.lognormal(np.log(P["mean_flats_per_building"]) - 0.5, 1.0)))
71	        sizes.append(s)
72	        total += s
73	    sizes[-1] -= total - P["n_flats"]
74	    nb = len(sizes)
75	    bld_block = rng.integers(0, B, nb)
76	    bld_eff = rng.normal(0, P["sd_building"], nb)
77	    bld_height = np.clip((np.array(sizes) / 4).astype(int) + 1, 1, 60)
78	
79	    bld = np.repeat(np.arange(nb), sizes)
80	    n = P["n_flats"]
81	    blk = bld_block[bld]
82	    sub = block_suburb[blk]
83	    bed = rng.choice(5, n, p=P["bed_p"])
84	    bath = np.where((bed >= 2) & (rng.random(n) < 0.4), 2, 1)
85	    park = (rng.random(n) < P["p_parking"]).astype(int)
86	    floor = rng.integers(0, bld_height[bld] + 1)
87	    floor_obs = np.where(rng.random(n) < P["p_floor_known"], floor, np.nan)
88	    unit_eff = rng.normal(0, P["sd_unit"], n)
89	    bed_e = np.array([P["bed_effect"][b] for b in range(5)])[bed]
90	    level = (np.log(P["base_rent"]) + suburb_eff[sub] + block_eff[blk] + env_eff[blk] + bld_eff[bld] + unit_eff
91	             + bed_e + P["bath2"] * (bath == 2) + P["floor_per_level"] * floor)
92	    flats = pd.DataFrame(dict(flat=np.arange(n), bld=bld, blk=blk, sub=sub, bed=bed, bath=bath, park=park,
93	                              floor_obs=floor_obs, fib=np.array(sizes)[bld], level=level,
94	                              block_map=block_map[blk], heat=z_heat[blk] + rng.normal(0, 0.2, n),
95	                              canopy=z_can[blk] + rng.normal(0, 0.2, n)))
96	
97	    mkt = market_index(len(MONTHS), rng)
98	    ever = rng.random(n) < P["p_ever_advertised"]
99	    lam = P["adverts_per_year"] * (TRAIN_END + 1) / 12.0
100	    k = np.where(ever, np.maximum(1, rng.poisson(lam, n)), 0)
101	    a_flat = np.repeat(np.arange(n), k)
102	    a_m = rng.integers(0, TRAIN_END + 1, a_flat.size)
103	    ads = pd.DataFrame(dict(flat=a_flat, m=a_m))
104	
105	    hist_flats = np.unique(a_flat)
106	    no_hist = np.setdiff1d(np.arange(n), hist_flats)
107	    n_h = int(round(P["n_test"] * p_hist_test))
108	    test_flats = np.concatenate([rng.choice(hist_flats, n_h, replace=False),
109	                                 rng.choice(no_hist, P["n_test"] - n_h, replace=False)])
110	    test = pd.DataFrame(dict(flat=test_flats, m=rng.choice(TEST_MONTHS, test_flats.size)))
111	
112	    def price(df):
113	        f = flats.loc[df.flat.values]
114	        lp = (f.level.values + P["parking"] * f.park.values + mkt[df.m.values]
115	              + suburb_growth[f["sub"].values] * df.m.values / 12.0 + rng.normal(0, P["sd_advert"], len(df)))
116	        return np.round(np.exp(lp) / 5) * 5
117	
118	    ads["price"] = price(ads)
119	    test["price"] = price(test)
120	    test["has_hist"] = np.isin(test.flat.values, hist_flats)
121	    return flats, ads, test
122	
123	
124	def repeat_index(ads):
125	    """Citywide monthly log index from repeat adverts (consecutive pairs), least squares, month 0 = 0."""
126	    a = ads.sort_values(["flat", "m"])
127	    prev = a.groupby("flat").shift(1)
128	    pr = a.assign(m0=prev.m, p0=prev.price).dropna()
129	    pr = pr[pr.m0 < pr.m]
130	    nm = TRAIN_END + 1
131	    rows = np.arange(len(pr))
132	    from scipy.sparse import coo_matrix
133	    from scipy.sparse.linalg import lsqr
134	    X = coo_matrix((np.r_[np.ones(len(pr)), -np.ones(len(pr))],
135	                    (np.r_[rows, rows], np.r_[pr.m.values.astype(int), pr.m0.values.astype(int)])), shape=(len(pr), nm)).tocsr()
136	    y = np.log(pr.price.values) - np.log(pr.p0.values)
137	    beta = lsqr(X[:, 1:], y, damp=1e-3)[0]
138	    idx = np.r_[0.0, beta]
139	    # carry forward to test months
140	    return np.r_[idx, np.full(len(MONTHS) - nm, idx[-1])]
141	
142	
143	def ladder(ads, flats, keys_df):
144	    recent = ads[ads.m > TRAIN_END - 12].merge(flats[["flat", "sub", "bed", "park"]], on="flat")
145	    out = np.full(len(keys_df), np.nan)
146	    for keys in (["sub", "bed", "park"], ["sub", "bed"], ["bed"]):
147	        g = recent.groupby(keys).price.agg(["median", "size"])
148	        g = g[g["size"] >= 10]["median"]
149	        vals = keys_df[keys].merge(g.rename("v").reset_index(), on=keys, how="left").v.values
150	        out = np.where(np.isnan(out), vals, out)
151	    return np.where(np.isnan(out), recent.price.median(), out)
152	
153	
154	def evaluate(pred, test):
155	    err = np.abs(pred - test.price.values)
156	    y = test.price.values
157	    r2 = 1 - np.sum((y - pred) ** 2) / np.sum((y - y.mean()) ** 2)
158	    nh = ~test.has_hist.values
159	    return dict(mae_med=np.median(err), within100=np.mean(err <= 100), r2=r2,
160	                mae_med_nohist=np.median(err[nh]) if nh.any() else np.nan)
161	
162	
163	def run_once(seed, heat_beta, canopy_beta, p_hist_test):
164	    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
165	    flats, ads, test = make_world(rng, heat_beta, canopy_beta, p_hist_test)
166	    idx = repeat_index(ads)
167	    tf = test.merge(flats, on="flat", how="left")
168	
169	    preds = {}
170	    m0 = ladder(ads, flats, tf)
171	    preds["M0"] = m0
172	
173	    last = ads.sort_values("m").groupby("flat").tail(1).set_index("flat")
174	    own = tf.flat.map(last.price)
175	    own_m = tf.flat.map(last.m)
176	    m1 = np.where(own.notna(), own * np.exp(idx[tf.m.values] - idx[own_m.fillna(0).astype(int).values]), m0)
177	    preds["M1"] = m1

"""Simulation study: which factors lower median absolute rent error, and is a heat effect detectable?

Synthetic City-of-Sydney-shaped world (all parameters are ASSUMPTIONS, listed in PARAMS / scenario grid).
Scoring mimics the task: 1,699 test adverts dated Aug-Sep 2026, training adverts <= 31 Jul 2026,
median absolute $ error ranks, share within $100 breaks ties, R^2 reported.

Methods (cumulative):
  M0  ladder median: suburb x bedrooms x parking -> suburb x bedrooms -> bedrooms (>=10 adverts, last 12 months)  [official example]
  M1  own last advert x citywide repeat-rent index; rows without own history use M0
  M2  M1 + no-history rows use same-building same-bedroom recent adverts (time-adjusted) when available
  M3  M2 + no-history rows use LightGBM on Microburbs-side features (suburb, bed, bath, parking, floor, flats_in_building,
      block rent map, building-comps median)
  M4  M3 + heat and canopy features
Run: python sim/sim_study.py [--quick]
"""
import argparse
import time

import lightgbm as lgb
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

PARAMS = dict(
    n_flats=65_777, n_suburbs=33, n_blocks=700, mean_flats_per_building=22,
    base_rent=520.0,
    sd_suburb=0.10, sd_block=0.07, sd_building=0.10, sd_unit=0.10, sd_advert=0.05,
    floor_per_level=0.006, parking=0.08, bath2=0.06,
    bed_effect={0: -0.37, 1: 0.0, 2: 0.32, 3: 0.63, 4: 0.92},  # from NSW bond data, CoS flats Aug-Sep 2026 medians
    bed_p=[0.10, 0.38, 0.40, 0.10, 0.02],
    p_parking=0.55, p_floor_known=0.52, p_ever_advertised=0.76, adverts_per_year=0.30,
    corr_heat_affluence=-0.4, corr_heat_canopy=-0.6, block_map_noise=0.03,
    n_test=1699,
)
# calibration target (NSW bond data, CoS flats): within postcode x bedrooms median abs log deviation 0.119
MONTHS = pd.period_range("2016-01", "2026-09", freq="M")
M_IDX = {p: i for i, p in enumerate(MONTHS)}
TRAIN_END = M_IDX[pd.Period("2026-07", "M")]
TEST_MONTHS = [M_IDX[pd.Period("2026-08", "M")], M_IDX[pd.Period("2026-09", "M")]]


def market_index(n_months, rng):
    t = np.arange(n_months) / 12.0
    idx = 0.03 * t
    covid = (np.arange(n_months) >= M_IDX[pd.Period("2020-04", "M")]) & (np.arange(n_months) <= M_IDX[pd.Period("2021-12", "M")])
    idx = idx - 0.12 * covid
    rebound = np.clip((np.arange(n_months) - M_IDX[pd.Period("2022-01", "M")]) / 24.0, 0, 1) * 0.08
    return idx + rebound + rng.normal(0, 0.005, n_months)


def make_world(rng, heat_beta, canopy_beta, p_hist_test):
    P = PARAMS
    S, B = P["n_suburbs"], P["n_blocks"]
    suburb_eff = rng.normal(0, P["sd_suburb"], S)
    suburb_growth = rng.normal(0, 0.01, S)
    block_suburb = rng.integers(0, S, B)
    block_eff = rng.normal(0, P["sd_block"], B)
    z_aff = block_eff / P["sd_block"]
    r = P["corr_heat_affluence"]
    z_heat = r * z_aff + np.sqrt(1 - r * r) * rng.normal(0, 1, B)
    rc = P["corr_heat_canopy"]
    z_can = rc * z_heat + np.sqrt(1 - rc * rc) * rng.normal(0, 1, B)
    env_eff = heat_beta * z_heat + canopy_beta * z_can
    # Microburbs block rent map is built from rents, so it already contains the environmental effect
    block_map = block_eff + env_eff + rng.normal(0, P["block_map_noise"], B)

    # buildings
    sizes = []
    total = 0
    while total < P["n_flats"]:
        s = max(1, int(rng.lognormal(np.log(P["mean_flats_per_building"]) - 0.5, 1.0)))
        sizes.append(s)
        total += s
    sizes[-1] -= total - P["n_flats"]
    nb = len(sizes)
    bld_block = rng.integers(0, B, nb)
    bld_eff = rng.normal(0, P["sd_building"], nb)
    bld_height = np.clip((np.array(sizes) / 4).astype(int) + 1, 1, 60)

    bld = np.repeat(np.arange(nb), sizes)
    n = P["n_flats"]
    blk = bld_block[bld]
    sub = block_suburb[blk]
    bed = rng.choice(5, n, p=P["bed_p"])
    bath = np.where((bed >= 2) & (rng.random(n) < 0.4), 2, 1)
    park = (rng.random(n) < P["p_parking"]).astype(int)
    floor = rng.integers(0, bld_height[bld] + 1)
    floor_obs = np.where(rng.random(n) < P["p_floor_known"], floor, np.nan)
    unit_eff = rng.normal(0, P["sd_unit"], n)
    bed_e = np.array([P["bed_effect"][b] for b in range(5)])[bed]
    level = (np.log(P["base_rent"]) + suburb_eff[sub] + block_eff[blk] + env_eff[blk] + bld_eff[bld] + unit_eff
             + bed_e + P["bath2"] * (bath == 2) + P["floor_per_level"] * floor)
    flats = pd.DataFrame(dict(flat=np.arange(n), bld=bld, blk=blk, sub=sub, bed=bed, bath=bath, park=park,
                              floor_obs=floor_obs, fib=np.array(sizes)[bld], level=level,
                              block_map=block_map[blk], heat=z_heat[blk] + rng.normal(0, 0.2, n),
                              canopy=z_can[blk] + rng.normal(0, 0.2, n)))

    mkt = market_index(len(MONTHS), rng)
    ever = rng.random(n) < P["p_ever_advertised"]
    lam = P["adverts_per_year"] * (TRAIN_END + 1) / 12.0
    k = np.where(ever, np.maximum(1, rng.poisson(lam, n)), 0)
    a_flat = np.repeat(np.arange(n), k)
    a_m = rng.integers(0, TRAIN_END + 1, a_flat.size)
    ads = pd.DataFrame(dict(flat=a_flat, m=a_m))

    hist_flats = np.unique(a_flat)
    no_hist = np.setdiff1d(np.arange(n), hist_flats)
    n_h = int(round(P["n_test"] * p_hist_test))
    test_flats = np.concatenate([rng.choice(hist_flats, n_h, replace=False),
                                 rng.choice(no_hist, P["n_test"] - n_h, replace=False)])
    test = pd.DataFrame(dict(flat=test_flats, m=rng.choice(TEST_MONTHS, test_flats.size)))

    def price(df):
        f = flats.loc[df.flat.values]
        lp = (f.level.values + P["parking"] * f.park.values + mkt[df.m.values]
              + suburb_growth[f["sub"].values] * df.m.values / 12.0 + rng.normal(0, P["sd_advert"], len(df)))
        return np.round(np.exp(lp) / 5) * 5

    ads["price"] = price(ads)
    test["price"] = price(test)
    test["has_hist"] = np.isin(test.flat.values, hist_flats)
    return flats, ads, test


def repeat_index(ads):
    """Citywide monthly log index from repeat adverts (consecutive pairs), least squares, month 0 = 0."""
    a = ads.sort_values(["flat", "m"])
    prev = a.groupby("flat").shift(1)
    pr = a.assign(m0=prev.m, p0=prev.price).dropna()
    pr = pr[pr.m0 < pr.m]
    nm = TRAIN_END + 1
    rows = np.arange(len(pr))
    from scipy.sparse import coo_matrix
    from scipy.sparse.linalg import lsqr
    X = coo_matrix((np.r_[np.ones(len(pr)), -np.ones(len(pr))],
                    (np.r_[rows, rows], np.r_[pr.m.values.astype(int), pr.m0.values.astype(int)])), shape=(len(pr), nm)).tocsr()
    y = np.log(pr.price.values) - np.log(pr.p0.values)
    beta = lsqr(X[:, 1:], y, damp=1e-3)[0]
    idx = np.r_[0.0, beta]
    # carry forward to test months
    return np.r_[idx, np.full(len(MONTHS) - nm, idx[-1])]


def ladder(ads, flats, keys_df):
    recent = ads[ads.m > TRAIN_END - 12].merge(flats[["flat", "sub", "bed", "park"]], on="flat")
    out = np.full(len(keys_df), np.nan)
    for keys in (["sub", "bed", "park"], ["sub", "bed"], ["bed"]):
        g = recent.groupby(keys).price.agg(["median", "size"])
        g = g[g["size"] >= 10]["median"]
        vals = keys_df[keys].merge(g.rename("v").reset_index(), on=keys, how="left").v.values
        out = np.where(np.isnan(out), vals, out)
    return np.where(np.isnan(out), recent.price.median(), out)


def evaluate(pred, test):
    err = np.abs(pred - test.price.values)
    y = test.price.values
    r2 = 1 - np.sum((y - pred) ** 2) / np.sum((y - y.mean()) ** 2)
    nh = ~test.has_hist.values
    return dict(mae_med=np.median(err), within100=np.mean(err <= 100), r2=r2,
                mae_med_nohist=np.median(err[nh]) if nh.any() else np.nan)


def run_once(seed, heat_beta, canopy_beta, p_hist_test):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    flats, ads, test = make_world(rng, heat_beta, canopy_beta, p_hist_test)
    idx = repeat_index(ads)
    tf = test.merge(flats, on="flat", how="left")

    preds = {}
    m0 = ladder(ads, flats, tf)
    preds["M0"] = m0

    last = ads.sort_values("m").groupby("flat").tail(1).set_index("flat")
    own = tf.flat.map(last.price)
    own_m = tf.flat.map(last.m)
    m1 = np.where(own.notna(), own * np.exp(idx[tf.m.values] - idx[own_m.fillna(0).astype(int).values]), m0)
    preds["M1"] = m1

    # same building, same bedrooms, last 24 months, time-adjusted to test month, excluding the flat itself
    a = ads[ads.m > TRAIN_END - 24].merge(flats[["flat", "bld", "bed", "park"]], on="flat")
    a["adj_log"] = np.log(a.price) - idx[a.m.values] - PARAMS["parking"] * 0  # parking handled below
    pk = a.groupby("park").adj_log.median()
    park_gap = pk.get(1, 0) - pk.get(0, 0)
    a["adj_log"] -= park_gap * a.park
    # leave-own-flat-out mean of other flats' adverts in the same building and bedroom count
    g_all = a.groupby(["bld", "bed"]).adj_log.agg(["sum", "size"]).rename(columns={"sum": "S", "size": "N"})
    g_flat = a.groupby("flat").adj_log.agg(["sum", "size"]).rename(columns={"sum": "Sf", "size": "Nf"})

    def loo_comp(df):
        x = df[["flat", "bld", "bed"]].merge(g_all.reset_index(), on=["bld", "bed"], how="left")
        x = x.merge(g_flat.reset_index(), on="flat", how="left").fillna({"Sf": 0, "Nf": 0, "S": 0, "N": 0})
        n_other = x.N - x.Nf
        return np.where(n_other > 0, (x.S - x.Sf) / n_other.replace(0, np.nan), np.nan)

    te_comp = loo_comp(tf)
    comp_pred = np.exp(te_comp + idx[tf.m.values] + park_gap * tf.park.values)
    nh = ~tf.has_hist.values
    m2 = np.where(nh & ~np.isnan(comp_pred), comp_pred, m1)
    preds["M2"] = m2

    # GBM for no-history rows: train on last-12-month adverts (time-adjusted to index), features Microburbs-side
    tr = ads[ads.m > TRAIN_END - 12].merge(flats, on="flat")
    tr_comp = loo_comp(tr)
    y_tr = np.log(tr.price.values) - idx[tr.m.values]
    base_cols = ["sub", "bed", "bath", "park", "floor_obs", "fib", "block_map"]
    Xb_tr = tr[base_cols].assign(comp=tr_comp)
    Xb_te = tf[base_cols].assign(comp=te_comp)
    env_cols = ["heat", "canopy"]
    out = {}
    for name, cols_extra in (("M3", []), ("M4", env_cols)):
        Xtr = pd.concat([Xb_tr, tr[cols_extra]], axis=1) if cols_extra else Xb_tr
        Xte = pd.concat([Xb_te, tf[cols_extra]], axis=1) if cols_extra else Xb_te
        mdl = lgb.LGBMRegressor(n_estimators=400, learning_rate=0.05, num_leaves=31, min_child_samples=30,
                                subsample=0.8, subsample_freq=1, colsample_bytree=0.9, verbose=-1, random_state=seed)
        mdl.fit(Xtr, y_tr, categorical_feature=["sub"])
        g = np.exp(mdl.predict(Xte) + idx[tf.m.values])
        out[name] = np.where(nh, g, m1)
    preds.update(out)

    res = {k: evaluate(v, test) for k, v in preds.items()}
    # paired bootstrap for M4 - M3 on median abs error (all rows and no-history rows)
    e3 = np.abs(preds["M3"] - test.price.values)
    e4 = np.abs(preds["M4"] - test.price.values)
    bs = []
    for _ in range(500):
        i = rng.integers(0, len(e3), len(e3))
        bs.append(np.median(e4[i]) - np.median(e3[i]))
    res["boot_M4_minus_M3"] = (np.percentile(bs, 2.5), np.percentile(bs, 97.5))
    res["n_nohist"] = int(nh.sum())
    return res


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--quick", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--seeds", type=int, default=3)
    args = ap.parse_args()
    grid = [(hb, cb, ph) for hb in (0.0, 0.01, 0.03) for cb in (0.0,) for ph in (0.6, 0.85)]
    if args.quick:
        grid = [(0.01, 0.0, 0.85)]
    rows = []
    for hb, cb, ph in grid:
        for s in range(args.seeds):
            t0 = time.time()
            r = run_once(s, hb, cb, ph)
            for m in ("M0", "M1", "M2", "M3", "M4"):
                rows.append(dict(heat_beta=hb, p_hist=ph, seed=s, method=m, **r[m]))
            lo, hi = r["boot_M4_minus_M3"]
            rows.append(dict(heat_beta=hb, p_hist=ph, seed=s, method="M4-M3 95%CI",
                             mae_med=np.nan, within100=np.nan, r2=np.nan, mae_med_nohist=np.nan, ci=f"[{lo:+.1f}, {hi:+.1f}]",
                             n_nohist=r["n_nohist"]))
            print(f"heat={hb} p_hist={ph} seed={s} done in {time.time()-t0:.1f}s", flush=True)
    df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    pd.set_option("display.width", 200)
    summ = (df[df.method != "M4-M3 95%CI"].groupby(["heat_beta", "p_hist", "method"])
            [["mae_med", "within100", "r2", "mae_med_nohist"]].mean().round(3))
    print(summ.to_string())
    print(df[df.method == "M4-M3 95%CI"][["heat_beta", "p_hist", "seed", "ci", "n_nohist"]].to_string(index=False))
    df.to_csv("sim/sim_results.csv", index=False)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Columns: Lodgement Date, Postcode, Dwelling Type (F flat/unit, H, T, O, U), Bedrooms, Weekly Rent. No address, no parking. Licence: page shows only "Copyright"; an older data.nsw record says CC BY (unverified for current files).

77	
78	**What wins most often, ranked:**
79	1. Validation that mimics the test split: a single latest-period holdout or time folds (1, 2, 4, 5, 7).
80	2. Gradient-boosted trees as the backbone: CatBoost, XGBoost or LightGBM (1, 2, 4, 7, 9).
81	3. Small, simple blends or stacks (1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9).
82	4. History-of-target and neighbour or group aggregate features (1, 2, 4, 7, 9).
83	5. Re-expressing the target relative to a baseline: a ratio or difference against a lag or capacity (2), or a centred target (1).
84	6. Snapping or rounding to known discrete values (3, 5, 6, 8).
85	
86	**For absolute-error and median metrics:**
87	- Losses: an L1/LAD stacker (8), training directly on the metric (6), or classification plus picking the value that minimises the metric (6).
88	- Snapping to discrete values gave the largest single gains (3, 8).
89	- Level corrections: weighted-mean subtraction (1) and per-group multipliers (10).
90	- No winner reported a specific bias correction for median error. That idea is my own suggestion and isn't backed by these sources.
91	
92	**What transfers to your 4-hour build:**
93	1. **Validate on a date cut.** Use the latest weeks before your cut-off as the holdout, matching the 1,699-advert test window, as winners 1, 2 and 7 did.
94	2. **Model rent relative to a baseline.** Predict log or ratio of rent against the flat's last advertised rent, adjusted for time. Fall back to the median of recent adverts in the same building and bedroom count, then the mesh-block median. This mirrors Enefit's ratio and difference targets.
95	3. **LightGBM or CatBoost with L1 or quantile-0.5 loss**, using median-based target encoding inside each fold (as in 9). Building and mesh-block keys are the categoricals.
96	4. **Snap and level-correct.** Round predictions to the $5 or $10 steps landlords actually advertise (as in 3, 5, 8). Check on the holdout whether that helps, and apply one global or per-suburb median-residual multiplier (as in 10).
97	5. **Blend 2ΓÇô3 models with L1 weights**: GBDT, a same-building/same-bedroom kNN median, and the last advert adjusted for time.
98	
99	**Wins a strict date cut-off would forbid:**
100	- Optiver Realized Volatility used the next period's value via a recovered time order.
101	- GoDaddy probed the public leaderboard.
102	- AMP's visit-schedule signal and Ventilator's reconstruction of the simulator exploited how the data was generated.
103	- S3E14 matched against the original dataset.
104	- For you: drop any advert dated after the cut-off, including same-building adverts, from features and target encodings.

| 3 | Ventilator Pressure (2021ΓÇá, Google Brain) | unverified (~2,650 per a search snippet) | MAE | simulated sequences | [team write-up](https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/ventilator-pressure-prediction/discussion/285256); rank 1 shown on [LB](https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/ventilator-pressure-prediction/leaderboard) |
| 4 | Optiver Realized Volatility (2021ΓÇá, Optiver) | 3,809 ([LB](https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/optiver-realized-volatility-prediction/leaderboard)) | RMSPE (unverified) | order book | [nyanp](https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/optiver-realized-volatility-prediction/discussion/274970) |
| 5 | GoDaddy Microbusiness Density (2023, GoDaddyΓÇá) | unverified | SMAPE ([index](https://oracleklein.github.io/kaggle-solutions/)) | monthly county panel | [kaggleqrdl](https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/godaddy-microbusiness-density-forecasting/writeups/kaggleqrdl-1-solution-generalization-with-linear-r) |
| 6 | AMP Parkinson's (2023ΓÇá, AMP PDΓÇá) | unverified | SMAPE+1 | longitudinal clinical visits | [Connecting Dotts](https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/amp-parkinsons-disease-progression-prediction/discussion/411505) |
| 7 | Rohlik Sales v2 (2025ΓÇá, Rohlik) | unverified (777 per an [X post](https://x.com/demorganize/status/1890729380231495842) that doesn't name the competition) | weighted MAE (unverified) | daily item ├ù warehouse sales | [Golden](https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/rohlik-sales-forecasting-challenge-v2/discussion/563215) |
| 8 | Playground S3E14 Blueberry Yield (2023, Kaggle) | unverified | MAE ([index](https://oracleklein.github.io/kaggle-solutions/)) | synthetic tabular | [Saharovskiy](https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/playground-series-s3e14/discussion/410627) |
| 9 | Playground S4E9 Used-Car Prices (2024ΓÇá, Kaggle) | unverified | RMSE | tabular price valuation | [Mart Preusse](https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/playground-series-s4e9/discussion/537052) |
| 10 | Playground S3E19 Mini-Course Sales (2023ΓÇá, Kaggle) | unverified | SMAPE ([index](https://oracleklein.github.io/kaggle-solutions/)) | daily sales by country | [JZ/ivyzang](https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/playground-series-s3e19/discussion/428311) (thin) |

## What each winner did

1. **Optiver Close**
   - Picked the top 300 features by CatBoost importance; history-of-target features were among them.
   - Single time holdout: "train on first 400 days and choose last 81 days as my holdout."
   - Blend of CatBoost 0.5, GRU 0.3 and Transformer 0.2, weights tuned on the holdout.
   - Retrained online every 12 days.
   - Post-processing: subtracted the weighted mean of predictions. Loss not stated.
   - Tool choice ([mlcontests 2024](https://mlcontests.com/state-of-machine-learning-competitions-2024/)): "CatBoost consumes less GPU and is also very fast."
2. **Enefit**
   - About 600 features, mostly lags, no feature selection.
   - Two target transforms: `(target ΓêÆ target_lag2)/installed_capacity` and `target/installed_capacity`. Raw targets "did not help."
   - Validation: trained on the first 500 days, the rest held out.
   - Models: 4 XGBoost plus 2 GRU, ensembled. Retrained monthly, which improved the test score from 53.66 to 52.31.
3. **Ventilator**
   - Models: LSTM on raw data, and LSTM + CNN-Transformer on engineered features. Blending "drops the MAE with more than 0.01."
   - Key move was snapping to discrete values: the target lies on a grid of 950 values, and matching against it "perfectly predict[s] 66% of the data."
   - Also reverse-engineered the PID controller that generated the data, which counts as "magic".
4. **Optiver Realized Volatility**
   - About 360 of the 600 features were nearest-neighbour aggregates across similar time IDs and stocks. These moved the score "from 0.21 to 0.19".
   - Used t-SNE to recover the hidden time order, then validated on a 4-fold time-series split.
   - Blend of LightGBM, MLP and 1D-CNN.
   - The write-up admits the "next time-id RV" feature is future information, i.e. leakage.
5. **GoDaddy**
   - Plain LinearRegression, one model per horizon, 3ΓÇô4 features each picked by greedy selection. "LR consistently resulted in more reliable CV scores" than GBDTs or neural nets.
   - Validation: the last non-overlapping window for each horizon.
   - Post-processing: "rounding based on active/populationΓÇª was a must."
   - Also probed the public leaderboard on volatile counties, which counts as leakage.
6. **AMP Parkinson's**
   - LightGBM as an 87-class classifier, averaged with a neural net trained directly on SMAPE+1.
   - Post-processing: chose the integer that minimises expected SMAPE, since the optimal predictions "are always integers."
   - The main signal was the visit-schedule pattern rather than biology, which counts as "magic". The team "fully ignores the results of the blood tests."
7. **Rohlik v2**
   - Features: mean-encodings of sales by weekday and other attributes, price/discount relative to the category, competing-product availability.
   - Validation: the two weeks just before the test period. Improvements there "would pretty much always improve" an earlier window as well.
   - Direct per-day LightGBM + XGBoost models ("28 models for the 14 day forecast"); blending added about 0.2.
   - What failed: Tweedie loss, recursive forecasting, outlier removal and segment-specific models.
   - Deliberately used no external data because of "potential for using leaky features."
8. **S3E14 (MAE)**
   - Stacked 8 out-of-fold models with an LAD (L1) regression on top.
   - The biggest gain came from snapping predictions to one of 776 known target values when feature patterns matched.
9. **S4E9 (car price valuation)**
   - Median-based target encoding of every categorical, recomputed "leakfreeΓÇª in each fold"; 20-fold CV.
   - A CatBoost classifier flags outliers above Q3 + 1.5┬╖IQR, and its out-of-fold output feeds the other models.
   - Final model is a neural net stacked on SVR, LightGBM, CatBoost and XGBoost outputs; it beat a Ridge blend.
10. **S3E19**
    - Main move was a per-country constant multiplier ("multiply the resultsΓÇª by a constant").
    - Validation and model details were not on the page.

## Synthesis

**What wins most often, ranked:**
1. Validation that mimics the test split: a single latest-period holdout or time folds (1, 2, 4, 5, 7).
2. Gradient-boosted trees as the backbone: CatBoost, XGBoost or LightGBM (1, 2, 4, 7, 9).
3. Small, simple blends or stacks (1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9).
4. History-of-target and neighbour or group aggregate features (1, 2, 4, 7, 9).
5. Re-expressing the target relative to a baseline: a ratio or difference against a lag or capacity (2), or a centred target (1).
6. Snapping or rounding to known discrete values (3, 5, 6, 8).

**For absolute-error and median metrics:**
- Losses: an L1/LAD stacker (8), training directly on the metric (6), or classification plus picking the value that minimises the metric (6).
- Snapping to discrete values gave the largest single gains (3, 8).
- Level corrections: weighted-mean subtraction (1) and per-group multipliers (10).
- No winner reported a specific bias correction for median error. That idea is my own suggestion and isn't backed by these sources.

**What transfers to your 4-hour build:**
1. **Validate on a date cut.** Use the latest weeks before your cut-off as the holdout, matching the 1,699-advert test window, as winners 1, 2 and 7 did.
2. **Model rent relative to a baseline.** Predict log or ratio of rent against the flat's last advertised rent, adjusted for time. Fall back to the median of recent adverts in the same building and bedroom count, then the mesh-block median. This mirrors Enefit's ratio and difference targets.
3. **LightGBM or CatBoost with L1 or quantile-0.5 loss**, using median-based target encoding inside each fold (as in 9). Building and mesh-block keys are the categoricals.
4. **Snap and level-correct.** Round predictions to the $5 or $10 steps landlords actually advertise (as in 3, 5, 8). Check on the holdout whether that helps, and apply one global or per-suburb median-residual multiplier (as in 10).
5. **Blend 2ΓÇô3 models with L1 weights**: GBDT, a same-building/same-bedroom kNN median, and the last advert adjusted for time.

**Wins a strict date cut-off would forbid:**
- Optiver Realized Volatility used the next period's value via a recovered time order.
- GoDaddy probed the public leaderboard.
- AMP's visit-schedule signal and Ventilator's reconstruction of the simulator exploited how the data was generated.
- S3E14 matched against the original dataset.
- For you: drop any advert dated after the cut-off, including same-building adverts, from features and target encodings.

"""Shared helpers for the public-data fetch scripts (Microburbs rents hackathon prep).

All scripts are re-runnable: python public-data/_scripts/<script>.py
Area: City of Sydney LGA + neighbours, lat -33.925..-33.855, lon 151.170..151.235.
"""
import json
import time
from pathlib import Path

import requests

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]          # public-data/
BBOX = dict(s=-33.925, w=151.170, n=-33.855, e=151.235)
ENVELOPE = f"{BBOX['w']},{BBOX['s']},{BBOX['e']},{BBOX['n']}"
UA = "MicroburbsHackathonPrep/1.0 (research; contact via hackathon team)"
S = requests.Session()
S.headers["User-Agent"] = UA


def get_json(url, params=None, method="GET", retries=4, timeout=180):
    for k in range(retries):
        try:
            if method == "GET":
                r = S.get(url, params=params, timeout=timeout)
            else:
                r = S.post(url, data=params, timeout=timeout)
            r.raise_for_status()
            d = r.json()
            if isinstance(d, dict) and "error" in d:
                raise RuntimeError(f"ArcGIS error {d['error']}")
            return d
        except Exception as ex:  # noqa: BLE001
            if k == retries - 1:
                raise

"""Land surface temperature, Sydney summer 2022-23 (NSW DPHI, part of the 2022 HVI dataset, CC BY 4.0).
The full GeoTIFF is ~309 MB; we read only the bbox window with HTTP range requests (GDAL /vsicurl/) after
resolving the data.nsw redirect to the signed S3 URL, and save a clipped GeoTIFF.
Run with the rents-heat venv:  rents-heat/.venv/Scripts/python.exe public-data/_scripts/fetch_lst.py
Output: public-data/heat/lst_sydney_2022-2023_summer_bbox.tif
"""
import os
import sys
import time

import requests
import rasterio
from rasterio.warp import transform_bounds
from rasterio.windows import from_bounds

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(__file__))
from common import BBOX, ROOT, UA  # noqa: E402

URL = ("https://datasets.seed.nsw.gov.au/dataset/08c39277-8b70-4c4d-905e-5c931c2eef08/resource/"
       "b081a8de-ca2e-4693-b961-706cd9f2c6ad/download/lst_sydney_2022-2023_summer.tif")
PAD = 0.01  # degrees of padding around the bbox

if __name__ == "__main__":
    t0 = time.time()
    r = requests.head(URL, headers={"User-Agent": UA}, allow_redirects=False, timeout=60)
    signed = r.headers.get("Location", URL)
    print("redirect status", r.status_code, "-> S3" if "amazonaws" in signed else "(no redirect)")
    os.environ["GDAL_HTTP_USERAGENT"] = UA
    os.environ["GDAL_DISABLE_READDIR_ON_OPEN"] = "EMPTY_DIR"
    os.environ["CPL_VSIL_CURL_ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS"] = ".tif"
    with rasterio.open("/vsicurl/" + signed) as src:
        print("crs", src.crs, "size", src.width, src.height, "res", src.res, "dtype", src.dtypes, "nodata", src.nodata,
              "tiled", src.profile.get("tiled"), "blocks", src.block_shapes)
        b = transform_bounds("EPSG:4326", src.crs, BBOX["w"] - PAD, BBOX["s"] - PAD, BBOX["e"] + PAD, BBOX["n"] + PAD)
        win = from_bounds(*b, transform=src.transform).round_offsets().round_lengths()
        data = src.read(window=win)
        prof = src.profile.copy()
        prof.update(width=data.shape[2], height=data.shape[1], transform=src.window_transform(win), compress="deflate",
                    tiled=True, blockxsize=256, blockysize=256)
        prof.pop("photometric", None)
        out = ROOT / "heat" / "lst_sydney_2022-2023_summer_bbox.tif"
        out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        with rasterio.open(out, "w", **prof) as dst:
            dst.write(data)
            dst.update_tags(source=URL, note="clipped bbox window via HTTP range reads", **src.tags())
    v = data[0][data[0] != (src.nodata if src.nodata is not None else -9999)]
    print("window", win, "shape", data.shape, "min/median/max", float(v.min()), float(sorted(v.ravel())[len(v)//2]), float(v.max()))
    print(f"saved {out} {out.stat().st_size/1e6:.2f} MB in {time.time()-t0:.0f}s")

content.text: Now a fetch script for ABS SA2 median rent (SA1 isn't in the Data API), using the SA2 codes from the HVI layer.

input.content:
"""ABS Census 2021 G02 'Median rent ($/weekly)' for SA2s intersecting the bbox, via the ABS Data API (SDMX).
SA1-level G02 is NOT offered by the Data API (only SA2+, LGA, POA, SAL...); SA1 would need the General Community
Profile DataPack (large zip), so SA1 was skipped (documented in MANIFEST). SA2 codes come from the HVI 2022 SA1
layer already downloaded (heat/hvi2022_sa1_bbox.geojson, field SA2_CODE21) - the SA1 polygons serve as the
SA1->SA2 allocation for the bbox.
Outputs: public-data/abs/c21_g02_sa2_median_rent_bbox.csv, abs/c21_g02_poa_median_rent_bbox.csv,
         abs/sa1_2021_bbox_from_hvi.csv (SA1 code, SA2 code, centroid)
"""
import io
import json

import pandas as pd

from common import ROOT, S

API = "https://data.api.abs.gov.au/rest/data"
POAS = ["2000", "2007", "2008", "2009", "2010", "2011", "2015", "2016", "2017", "2018", "2021", "2037", "2042",
        "2043", "2050", "2006", "2019", "2020", "2033", "2060", "2061"]


def fetch(flow, regions, region_type):
    key = f"6.{'+'.join(regions)}.{region_type}.1"
    url = f"{API}/ABS,{flow},1.0.0/{key}"
    r = S.get(url, params={"format": "csvfilewithlabels"}, headers={"Accept": "application/vnd.sdmx.data+csv;labels=both"},
              timeout=120)
    r.raise_for_status()
    df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(r.text))

"""Build public-data/_derived/buildings_features.parquet (+ .csv) - one row per OSM residential building in the bbox.
Run with the rents-heat venv (shapely, pyproj, rasterio, scipy):
    rents-heat/.venv/Scripts/python.exe public-data/_scripts/build_features.py

Residential rule (documented choice):
  res_rule = 'apt'     building in {apartments, residential, flats}
             'yes_ge3' building = yes AND levels >= 3 AND no non-residential tag (shop, office, amenity, tourism,
                       craft, healthcare, leisure, building:use in commercial/retail/office) -> may still be offices
                       in the CBD; kept but flagged so the user can drop them.
  Houses/terraces are excluded (the task is flats).
levels = building:levels (numeric part); if missing and height present, round(height/3.1) (levels_src='height').
All distances computed in EPSG:7856 (GDA2020 / MGA zone 56), metres.
"""
import json
import re
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import rasterio
import shapely
from pyproj import Transformer
from scipy.spatial import cKDTree
from shapely.geometry import LineString, Point, Polygon, shape
from shapely.ops import polygonize, transform, unary_union

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
OUT = ROOT / "_derived"
OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
TO_M = Transformer.from_crs("EPSG:4326", "EPSG:7856", always_xy=True).transform
NONRES = ("shop", "office", "amenity", "tourism", "craft", "healthcare", "leisure")


def num(s):
    if s is None:
        return np.nan
    m = re.search(r"\d+(\.\d+)?", str(s).replace(",", "."))
    return float(m.group()) if m else np.nan


def osm_polys():
    d = json.load(open(ROOT / "osm" / "osm_buildings_bbox.json", encoding="utf-8"))
    rel_path = ROOT / "osm" / "osm_building_relations_bbox.json"
    rels = {}
    if rel_path.exists():
        for e in json.load(open(rel_path, encoding="utf-8"))["elements"]:
            rels[e["id"]] = e
    rows = []
    for e in d["elements"]:
        t = e.get("tags", {})
        g = None
        if e["type"] == "way" and len(e.get("geometry", [])) >= 4:
            g = Polygon([(p["lon"], p["lat"]) for p in e["geometry"]])
        elif e["type"] == "relation" and e["id"] in rels:
            lines = [LineString([(p["lon"], p["lat"]) for p in m["geometry"]]) for m in rels[e["id"]].get("members", [])
                     if m.get("role") == "outer" and len(m.get("geometry", [])) >= 2]
            polys = list(polygonize(unary_union(lines))) if lines else []
            if polys:
                g = unary_union(polys)
        if g is None or g.is_empty:
            continue
        if not g.is_valid:
            g = g.buffer(0)
        rows.append(dict(osm_type=e["type"], osm_id=e["id"], tags=t, geom=g))
    print(len(rows), "building polygons (", sum(r["osm_type"] == "relation" for r in rows), "relations)")
    return rows, d.get("osm3s", {}).get("timestamp_osm_base")


def main():
    t0 = time.time()
    rows, osm_ts = osm_polys()
    df = pd.DataFrame(dict(osm_type=[r["osm_type"] for r in rows], osm_id=[r["osm_id"] for r in rows]))
    tags = [r["tags"] for r in rows]
    df["building"] = [t.get("building") for t in tags]
    lv = np.array([num(t.get("building:levels")) for t in tags])
    ht = np.array([num(t.get("height")) for t in tags])
    df["levels_tag"] = lv
    df["height_m"] = ht
    df["levels"] = np.where(np.isnan(lv), np.round(ht / 3.1), lv)
    df["levels_src"] = np.where(~np.isnan(lv), "building:levels", np.where(~np.isnan(ht), "height", None))
    df["addr_housenumber"] = [t.get("addr:housenumber") for t in tags]
    df["addr_street"] = [t.get("addr:street") for t in tags]
    df["addr_suburb"] = [t.get("addr:suburb") or t.get("addr:city") for t in tags]
    df["addr_postcode"] = [t.get("addr:postcode") for t in tags]
    df["name"] = [t.get("name") for t in tags]
    df["start_date_osm"] = [t.get("start_date") for t in tags]
    nonres = np.array([any(k in t for k in NONRES) or t.get("building:use") in ("commercial", "retail", "office")
                       for t in tags])
    geoms_ll = [r["geom"] for r in rows]
    geoms_m = [transform(TO_M, g) for g in geoms_ll]
    cen_m = np.array([[g.centroid.x, g.centroid.y] for g in geoms_m])
    cen_ll = [g.centroid for g in geoms_ll]
    df["lon"] = [c.x for c in cen_ll]
    df["lat"] = [c.y for c in cen_ll]
    df["footprint_m2"] = [g.area for g in geoms_m]

    # neighbour max levels within 100 m (all buildings with known levels, excluding self)
    tree = cKDTree(cen_m)
    has = ~np.isnan(df.levels.values)
    lvv = df.levels.values
    nmax = np.full(len(df), np.nan)
    for i, nb in enumerate(tree.query_ball_point(cen_m, r=100.0)):
        vals = [lvv[j] for j in nb if j != i and has[j]]
        if vals:
            nmax[i] = max(vals)
    df["neighbour_max_levels_100m"] = nmax
    df["n_buildings_100m"] = [len(nb) - 1 for nb in tree.query_ball_point(cen_m, r=100.0)]

    # residential selection
    b = df.building.values
    is_apt = np.isin(b, ["apartments", "residential", "flats"])
    is_yes3 = (b == "yes") & (df.levels.values >= 3) & ~nonres
    df["res_rule"] = np.where(is_apt, "apt", np.where(is_yes3, "yes_ge3", None))
    sel = df.res_rule.notna().values
    print("residential:", sel.sum(), "of", len(df), pd.Series(df.res_rule[sel]).value_counts().to_dict())
    R = df[sel].reset_index(drop=True)
    Rg_m = [geoms_m[i] for i in np.where(sel)[0]]
    Rc_m = shapely.points(cen_m[sel])

    # strata plans
    sp = json.load(open(ROOT / "cadastre" / "sp_lots_bbox.geojson", encoding="utf-8"))["features"]
    sp_geom = [transform(TO_M, shape(f["geometry"]).buffer(0)) for f in sp]
    sp_pn = np.array([f["properties"]["plannumber"] for f in sp])
    sp_cd = pd.to_datetime([f["properties"]["createdate"] for f in sp], unit="ms")
    st = shapely.STRtree(sp_geom)
    pi, gi = st.query(Rc_m, predicate="within")
    first = pd.Series(gi, index=pi).groupby(level=0).first()
    R["sp_plannumber"] = pd.Series(sp_pn[first.values], index=first.index).reindex(range(len(R))).values
    R["sp_createdate"] = pd.Series(sp_cd[first.values], index=first.index).reindex(range(len(R))).values
    shrunk = [g.buffer(-1.0) if g.area > 20 else g for g in Rg_m]
    pi2, gi2 = st.query(shrunk, predicate="intersects")
    R["n_sp_plans"] = pd.Series(1, index=pi2).groupby(level=0).size().reindex(range(len(R))).fillna(0).astype(int).values
    # nearest SP within 15 m when centroid is not inside one (centroid can fall in a courtyard)
    miss = np.where(pd.isna(R.sp_plannumber.values))[0]
    if len(miss):
        idx = st.nearest([Rc_m[i] for i in miss])
        d = shapely.distance(np.array(Rc_m)[miss], np.array(sp_geom, dtype=object)[idx])
        ok = d <= 15
        R.loc[miss[ok], "sp_plannumber"] = sp_pn[idx[ok]]
        R.loc[miss[ok], "sp_createdate"] = sp_cd[idx[ok]]
        R["sp_match"] = np.where(pd.notna(R.sp_plannumber), "centroid_within", None)
        R.loc[miss[ok], "sp_match"] = "nearest<=15m"

    # stations
    stn = json.load(open(ROOT / "osm" / "osm_stations_bbox.json", encoding="utf-8"))["elements"]
    srows = []
    for e in stn:
        c = e.get("center") or {"lat": e.get("lat"), "lon": e.get("lon")}
        if c.get("lat") is None:
            continue
        t = e.get("tags", {})
        kind = ("light_rail" if t.get("railway") == "tram_stop" or t.get("light_rail") == "yes" or t.get("tram") == "yes"
                else "rail_metro")
        x, y = TO_M(c["lon"], c["lat"])
        srows.append((x, y, kind, t.get("name")))
    S = pd.DataFrame(srows, columns=["x", "y", "kind", "name"])
    xy = np.c_[[p.x for p in Rc_m], [p.y for p in Rc_m]]
    R["dist_station_m"] = cKDTree(S[["x", "y"]].values).query(xy)[0]
    rm = S[S.kind == "rail_metro"]
    R["dist_rail_metro_m"] = cKDTree(rm[["x", "y"]].values).query(xy)[0]

    # water: coastline lines + water polygons >= 5 ha (harbour/bays/large ponds); small ponds ignored
    wat = json.load(open(ROOT / "osm" / "osm_water_bbox.json", encoding="utf-8"))["elements"]
    wg = []
    for e in wat:
        t = e.get("tags", {})
        if e["type"] == "way" and e.get("geometry"):
            coords = [(p["lon"], p["lat"]) for p in e["geometry"]]
            if t.get("natural") == "coastline":
                wg.append(transform(TO_M, LineString(coords)))
            elif len(coords) >= 4 and coords[0] == coords[-1]:
                pg = transform(TO_M, Polygon(coords).buffer(0))
                if pg.area >= 5e4:
                    wg.append(pg)
        elif e["type"] == "relation":
            lines = [LineString([(p["lon"], p["lat"]) for p in m["geometry"]]) for m in e.get("members", [])
                     if m.get("role") == "outer" and m.get("geometry")]
            if lines:
                polys = list(polygonize(unary_union(lines)))
                if polys:
                    pg = transform(TO_M, unary_union(polys))
                    if pg.area >= 5e4:
                        wg.append(pg)
    W = unary_union(wg)
    R["dist_water_m"] = shapely.distance(np.array(Rc_m), W)
    print("water geoms", len(wg))

    # LST raster (point sample at centroid, ~30 m pixels)
    with rasterio.open(ROOT / "heat" / "lst_sydney_2022-2023_summer_bbox.tif") as src:
        vals = np.array([v[0] for v in src.sample(list(zip(R.lon, R.lat)))], dtype=float)
    R["lst_c"] = vals

    def poly_join(path, fields, prefix=""):
        fc = json.load(open(path, encoding="utf-8"))["features"]
        g = [transform(TO_M, shape(f["geometry"]).buffer(0)) for f in fc if f.get("geometry")]
        props = [f["properties"] for f in fc if f.get("geometry")]
        t = shapely.STRtree(g)
        a, b_ = t.query(Rc_m, predicate="within")
        m = pd.Series(b_, index=a).groupby(level=0).first().reindex(range(len(R)))
        out = {}
        for fsrc, fdst in fields.items():
            col = np.array([p.get(fsrc) for p in props], dtype=object)
            out[fdst] = [col[int(k)] if pd.notna(k) else None for k in m.values]
        return out

    for k, v in poly_join(ROOT / "canopy" / "canopy2022_mmb_bbox.geojson",
                          {"PCT_TREE": "canopy_mmb_pct", "Canopy_Percentage": "canopy_mmb_pct_alt",
                           "MMB_CODE": "mmb_code", "MB_CODE16": "mb_code16_canopy"}).items():
        R[k] = v
    for k, v in poly_join(ROOT / "heat" / "uhi2016_mb_bbox.geojson",
                          {"UHI_16_m": "uhi16_mmb", "MB_CODE16": "mb_code16", "SA1_MAIN16": "sa1_main16"}).items():
        R[k] = v
    for k, v in poly_join(ROOT / "heat" / "hvi2022_sa1_bbox.geojson",
                          {"LST": "lst_sa1_hvi", "SA1_2021_AUST_GDA2020_SA1_CODE2": "sa1_code21", "SA2_CODE21": "sa2_code21",
                           "SA2_NAME21": "sa2_name21", "Per_Tree": "tree_pct_sa1_hvi"}).items():
        R[k] = v
    abs2 = pd.read_csv(ROOT / "abs" / "c21_g02_sa2_median_rent_bbox.csv")
    abs2 = abs2.set_index(abs2.REGION.astype(str)).OBS_VALUE
    R["abs_sa2_median_rent_2021"] = R.sa2_code21.map(lambda s: abs2.get(str(s)) if s is not None else np.nan)
    for c in ["canopy_mmb_pct", "canopy_mmb_pct_alt", "uhi16_mmb", "lst_sa1_hvi", "tree_pct_sa1_hvi", "abs_sa2_median_rent_2021"]:
        R[c] = pd.to_numeric(R[c], errors="coerce")
    R["sp_createdate"] = pd.to_datetime(R.sp_createdate)
    R["osm_timestamp_base"] = osm_ts

    R.to_parquet(OUT / "buildings_features.parquet", index=False)
    R.to_csv(OUT / "buildings_features.csv", index=False)

    # coverage and correlations
    cols = ["footprint_m2", "levels", "neighbour_max_levels_100m", "sp_plannumber", "sp_createdate", "n_sp_plans",
            "dist_station_m", "dist_rail_metro_m", "dist_water_m", "lst_c", "canopy_mmb_pct", "uhi16_mmb",
            "lst_sa1_hvi", "abs_sa2_median_rent_2021"]
    cov = pd.DataFrame({"pct_non_null_all": R[cols].notna().mean() * 100,
                        "pct_non_null_apt": R.loc[R.res_rule == "apt", cols].notna().mean() * 100}).round(1)
    cov.loc["n_sp_plans>=2 (multi-plan share)", :] = [(R.n_sp_plans >= 2).mean() * 100,
                                                      (R.loc[R.res_rule == "apt", "n_sp_plans"] >= 2).mean() * 100]
    num_cols = [c for c in cols if c != "sp_createdate"]
    C = R[num_cols].assign(sp_create_year=R.sp_createdate.dt.year + R.sp_createdate.dt.dayofyear / 365.25)
    corr = C.corr(method="spearman").round(2)
    cov.to_csv(OUT / "buildings_features_coverage.csv")
    corr.to_csv(OUT / "buildings_features_corr_spearman.csv")
    desc = R[num_cols].describe().T.round(2)
    desc.to_csv(OUT / "buildings_features_describe.csv")
    with open(OUT / "buildings_features_summary.md", "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(f"# buildings_features summary\n\nRows: {len(R)} ({R.res_rule.value_counts().to_dict()}); OSM base {osm_ts}\n\n")
        f.write("## Coverage (% non-null)\n\n" + cov.to_markdown() + "\n\n## Describe\n\n" + desc.to_markdown() +
                "\n\n## Spearman correlations\n\n" + corr.to_markdown() + "\n")
    pd.set_option("display.width", 250)
    print(cov.to_string())
    print(corr.to_string())
    print(f"done in {time.time()-t0:.0f}s")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

from shapely.geometry import LineString, Point, Polygon, shape

    sp_pn = np.array([f["properties"]["plannumber"] for f in sp])
    sp_cd = pd.to_datetime([f["properties"]["createdate"] for f in sp], unit="ms")
    st = shapely.STRtree(sp_geom)

    shrunk = [g.buffer(-1.0) if g.area > 20 else g for g in Rg_m]

    R["n_sp_plans"] = pd.Series(1, index=pi2).groupby(level=0).size().reindex(range(len(R))).fillna(0).astype(int).values

    miss = np.where(pd.isna(R.sp_plannumber.values))[0]
    if len(miss):
        idx = st.nearest([Rc_m[i] for i in miss])
        d = shapely.distance(np.array(Rc_m)[miss], np.array(sp_geom, dtype=object)[idx])
        ok = d <= 15
        R.loc[miss[ok], "sp_plannumber"] = sp_pn[idx[ok]]
        R.loc[miss[ok], "sp_createdate"] = sp_cd[idx[ok]]
        R["sp_match"] = np.where(pd.notna(R.sp_plannumber), "centroid_within", None)
        R.loc[miss[ok], "sp_match"] = "nearest<=15m"

        fc = json.load(open(path, encoding="utf-8"))["features"]
        g = [transform(TO_M, shape(f["geometry"]).buffer(0)) for f in fc if f.get("geometry")]
        props = [f["properties"] for f in fc if f.get("geometry")]
        t = shapely.STRtree(g)

        m = pd.Series(b_, index=a).groupby(level=0).first().reindex(range(len(R)))

        for fsrc, fdst in fields.items():

                          {"PCT_TREE": "canopy_mmb_pct", "Canopy_Percentage": "canopy_mmb_pct_alt",

    for k, v in poly_join(ROOT / "heat" / "uhi2016_mb_bbox.geojson",

    abs2 = abs2.set_index(abs2.REGION.astype(str)).OBS_VALUE
    R["abs_sa2_median_rent_2021"] = R.sa2_code21.map(lambda s: abs2.get(str(s)) if s is not None else np.nan)
    for c in ["canopy_mmb_pct", "canopy_mmb_pct_alt", "uhi16_mmb", "lst_sa1_hvi", "tree_pct_sa1_hvi", "abs_sa2_median_rent_2021"]:

    R.to_csv(OUT / "buildings_features.csv", index=False)

    # coverage and correlations
    cols = ["footprint_m2", "levels", "neighbour_max_levels_100m", "sp_plannumber", "sp_createdate", "n_sp_plans",
            "dist_station_m", "dist_rail_metro_m", "dist_water_m", "lst_c", "canopy_mmb_pct", "uhi16_mmb",

    cov.to_csv(OUT / "buildings_features_coverage.csv")
    corr.to_csv(OUT / "buildings_features_corr_spearman.csv")
    desc = R[num_cols].describe().T.round(2)
    desc.to_csv(OUT / "buildings_features_describe.csv")
    with open(OUT / "buildings_features_summary.md", "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:

                "\n\n## Spearman correlations\n\n" + corr.to_markdown() + "\n")
    pd.set_option("display.width", 250)
    print(cov.to_string())
    print(corr.to_string())
    print(f"done in {time.time()-t0:.0f}s")

    sys.exit(main())

    R["dist_station_m"] = cKDTree(S[["x", "y"]].values).query(xy)[0]
    rm = S[S.kind == "rail_metro"]
    R["dist_rail_metro_m"] = cKDTree(rm[["x", "y"]].values).query(xy)[0]

    # water: coastline lines + water polygons >= 5 ha (harbour/bays/large ponds); small ponds ignored
    wat = json.load(open(ROOT / "osm" / "osm_water_bbox.json", encoding="utf-8"))["elements"]
    wg = []
    for e in wat:
        t = e.get("tags", {})
        if e["type"] == "way" and e.get("geometry"):
            coords = [(p["lon"], p["lat"]) for p in e["geometry"]]
            if t.get("natural") == "coastline":
                wg.append(transform(TO_M, LineString(coords)))
            elif len(coords) >= 4 and coords[0] == coords[-1]:
                pg = transform(TO_M, Polygon(coords).buffer(0))
                if pg.area >= 5e4:
                    wg.append(pg)
        elif e["type"] == "relation":
            lines = [LineString([(p["lon"], p["lat"]) for p in m["geometry"]]) for m in e.get("members", [])
                     if m.get("role") == "outer" and m.get("geometry")]
            if lines:
                polys = list(polygonize(unary_union(lines)))
                if polys:
                    pg = transform(TO_M, unary_union(polys))
                    if pg.area >= 5e4:
                        wg.append(pg)
    W = unary_union(wg)
    R["dist_water_m"] = shapely.distance(np.array(Rc_m), W)
    print("water geoms", len(wg))

    # LST raster (point sample at centroid, ~30 m pixels)
    with rasterio.open(ROOT / "heat" / "lst_sydney_2022-2023_summer_bbox.tif") as src:
        vals = np.array([v[0] for v in src.sample(list(zip(R.lon, R.lat)))], dtype=float)
    R["lst_c"] = vals

    def poly_join(path, fields, prefix=""):
        fc = json.load(open(path, encoding="utf-8"))["features"]
        g = [transform(TO_M, shape(f["geometry"]).buffer(0)) for f in fc if f.get("geometry")]
        props = [f["properties"] for f in fc if f.get("geometry")]
        t = shapely.STRtree(g)
        a, b_ = t.query(Rc_m, predicate="within")
        m = pd.Series(b_, index=a).groupby(level=0).first().reindex(range(len(R)))
        out = {}
        for fsrc, fdst in fields.items():
            col = np.array([p.get(fsrc) for p in props], dtype=object)
            out[fdst] = [col[int(k)] if pd.notna(k) else None for k in m.values]
        return out

    for k, v in poly_join(ROOT / "canopy" / "canopy2022_mmb_bbox.geojson",
                          {"PCT_TREE": "canopy_mmb_pct", "Canopy_Percentage": "canopy_mmb_pct_alt",
                           "MMB_CODE": "mmb_code", "MB_CODE16": "mb_code16_canopy"}).items():
        R[k] = v
    for k, v in poly_join(ROOT / "heat" / "uhi2016_mb_bbox.geojson",
                          {"UHI_16_m": "uhi16_mmb", "MB_CODE16": "mb_code16", "SA1_MAIN16": "sa1_main16"}).items():
        R[k] = v
    for k, v in poly_join(ROOT / "heat" / "hvi2022_sa1_bbox.geojson",
                          {"LST": "lst_sa1_hvi", "SA1_2021_AUST_GDA2020_SA1_CODE2": "sa1_code21", "SA2_CODE21": "sa2_code21",
                           "SA2_NAME21": "sa2_name21", "Per_Tree": "tree_pct_sa1_hvi"}).items():
        R[k] = v
    abs2 = pd.read_csv(ROOT / "abs" / "c21_g02_sa2_median_rent_bbox.csv")
    abs2 = abs2.set_index(abs2.REGION.astype(str)).OBS_VALUE
    R["abs_sa2_median_rent_2021"] = R.sa2_code21.map(lambda s: abs2.get(str(s)) if s is not None else np.nan)
    for c in ["canopy_mmb_pct", "canopy_mmb_pct_alt", "uhi16_mmb", "lst_sa1_hvi", "tree_pct_sa1_hvi", "abs_sa2_median_rent_2021"]:
        R[c] = pd.to_numeric(R[c], errors="coerce")
    R["sp_createdate"] = pd.to_datetime(R.sp_createdate)
    R["osm_timestamp_base"] = osm_ts

    R.to_parquet(OUT / "buildings_features.parquet", index=False)
    R.to_csv(OUT / "buildings_features.csv", index=False)

    # coverage and correlations
    cols = ["footprint_m2", "levels", "neighbour_max_levels_100m", "sp_plannumber", "sp_createdate", "n_sp_plans",
            "dist_station_m", "dist_rail_metro_m", "dist_water_m", "lst_c", "canopy_mmb_pct", "uhi16_mmb",
            "lst_sa1_hvi", "abs_sa2_median_rent_2021"]
    cov = pd.DataFrame({"pct_non_null_all": R[cols].notna().mean() * 100,
                        "pct_non_null_apt": R.loc[R.res_rule == "apt", cols].notna().mean() * 100}).round(1)
    cov.loc["n_sp_plans>=2 (multi-plan share)", :] = [(R.n_sp_plans >= 2).mean() * 100,
                                                      (R.loc[R.res_rule == "apt", "n_sp_plans"] >= 2).mean() * 100]
    num_cols = [c for c in cols if c != "sp_createdate"]
    C = R[num_cols].assign(sp_create_year=R.sp_createdate.dt.year + R.sp_createdate.dt.dayofyear / 365.25)
    corr = C.corr(method="spearman").round(2)
    cov.to_csv(OUT / "buildings_features_coverage.csv")
    corr.to_csv(OUT / "buildings_features_corr_spearman.csv")
    desc = R[num_cols].describe().T.round(2)
    desc.to_csv(OUT / "buildings_features_describe.csv")
    with open(OUT / "buildings_features_summary.md", "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(f"# buildings_features summary\n\nRows: {len(R)} ({R.res_rule.value_counts().to_dict()}); OSM base {osm_ts}\n\n")
        f.write("## Coverage (% non-null)\n\n" + cov.to_markdown() + "\n\n## Describe\n\n" + desc.to_markdown() +
                "\n\n## Spearman correlations\n\n" + corr.to_markdown() + "\n")
    pd.set_option("display.width", 250)
    print(cov.to_string())
    print(corr.to_string())
    print(f"done in {time.time()-t0:.0f}s")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# Data Visualization

A chart is **read by people and executed by you**. This skill turns "make it look
good" into a procedure with checks, so the result is right by construction rather
than by taste.

**The method here is design-system-agnostic.** Nothing in the procedure, the form
heuristic, the six checks, or the mark specs is specific to one product. A design
system supplies a small set of *parameters* (its ramps, a categorical order, a
diverging pair, a status palette, a texture, its surfaces, its filter components);
the method consumes them unchanged. A **validated default palette** is the
reference instance, fully specified in `references/palette.md`. To target your
brand, read that file's structure and substitute its values - touch nothing else.

> The single most important habit: **the color part is computable, so compute it.**
> Never eyeball whether a palette is colorblind-safe - run `scripts/validate_palette.js`.

## The procedure - do these in order

Color comes LAST. Most bad charts pick colors first.

1. **Pick the form.** What is the data's job - magnitude, identity, polarity, a
   single headline, change-over-time? The job picks the chart type, and sometimes
   the answer is *not a chart* (a stat tile or hero number). -> `references/choosing-a-form.md`
2. **Assign color by the job it does.** Categorical (identity), sequential
   (magnitude), diverging (polarity), or status (state) - each has one rule.
   Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled. -> `references/color-formula.md`
3. **VALIDATE the palette - run the script, don't reason about Delta E.**
   `node scripts/validate_palette.js "<hex,hex,...>" --mode light` (relative to
   this skill's base directory - or load it as `<script type="module">` in the
   chart's own page, where it reads
   `data-palette` off `<body>` and logs a `console.table` report). It returns
   pass/fail on the lightness band, chroma floor, adjacent-pair CVD separation,
   the normal-vision floor, and contrast. Fix anything that FAILs before continuing. Re-run for
   `--mode dark` with that mode's surface.
4. **Apply mark specs & spacers.** Thin marks, 4px rounded data-ends anchored to
   the baseline, 2px lines, >=8px markers, a 2px surface gap between fills (stacked
   segments and adjacent bars alike) and a 2px surface ring on overlapping marks,
   selective direct labels. -> `references/marks-and-anatomy.md`
5. **Add the hover layer - by default.** An HTML/SVG chart *is* interactive; ship
   a crosshair+tooltip on line/area and a per-mark hover tooltip on bar/dot/cell.
   The only form that skips it is a bare stat tile with no plot. Hit targets bigger
   than the mark; filters in one row above the charts. -> `references/interaction.md`
6. **Final accessibility pass.** For >= 2 series a legend is always present and <= 4
   are also direct-labeled (a single series needs no legend box - the title names
   it), so identity is never color-alone; a table view exists; dark mode is **selected** - its own
   steps from the same ramps, validated against the dark surface, not an automatic
   flip; texture is available for the CVD/print/forced-colors case.
7. **Render it and look at it.** The validator checks color, not layout - open or
   screenshot the output and eyeball it for label collisions, geometry, and overflow
   before calling it done.

Then check the result against **`references/anti-patterns.md`** - it is the catalog
of what goes wrong. If your chart matches an entry, it's wrong.

## Non-negotiables (true in every design system)

- **Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled.** A 9th series is never a
  generated hue - it folds into "Other," small multiples, or composite encoding.
- **One axis.** Never a dual-axis chart (two y-scales). Two measures of different
  scale -> two charts, small multiples, or indexed to a common base. *(This is the
  #1 chart mistake - see anti-patterns.)*
- **Color follows the entity, never its rank.** A filter that changes the series
  count must not repaint the survivors.
- **Sequential = one hue, light->dark. Diverging = two hues + a neutral gray
  midpoint.** Never a rainbow; never a hue at the diverging midpoint.
- **Run the validator before shipping any categorical palette.** CVD Delta E >= 8 is the
  target (OKLab ×100); 6-8 is a floor that is legal ONLY with secondary encoding. A
  normal-vision floor below 15 is a hard FAIL - full-color readers can't tell the
  pair apart; re-step it on the adjacent pairlist (secondary encoding does not excuse
  this one); under `--pairs all` cut series or facet instead - see check 4. A contrast WARN
  obligates visible labels or a table view - it is not dismissable.
- **Thin marks; a legend always present for >= 2 series (none for one), with
  selective direct labels (never a number on every point); recessive grid/axes.**
  One exception, legend kept: the tall segmented bar (*Figures* in `references/marks-and-anatomy.md`).
- **Text wears text tokens, never the series color** - values, labels, and legends
  stay in primary/secondary/muted ink; a colored mark beside them carries identity.
- **Status colors are reserved** (good/warning/serious/critical) and never reused
  for "series 4"; they ship with an icon + label, never color alone.

## Plugging in a design system

The method is invariant; only these parameters change per system. The reference
instance - every value filled in - is `references/palette.md`.

| Parameter | What the system provides |
|---|---|
| **Ramps** | the hue scales (named steps) the palette draws from |
| **Categorical theme** | the fixed hue order (a named theme); default + alternates |
| **Sequential hue** | the default single hue for magnitude |
| **Diverging pair** | two warm/cool poles + a neutral midpoint |
| **Status palette** | good / warning / serious / critical - steps distinct from categorical |
| **Texture fill** | one directional hand-drawn fill, used at 45° / 135° |
| **Surfaces** | light & dark chart-surface colors (the validator needs these) |
| **Filter controls** | date-range & dimension controls (behavioral spec in `interaction.md`) |

To onboard a new system: fill those rows, feed its ramps to the validator, and let
it snap each slot to the nearest passing step. Structure and rules stay as written.

## Reference files

| File | What it answers |
|------|-----------------|
| `references/choosing-a-form.md` | Which chart type / is it even a chart? |
| `references/color-formula.md` | The four jobs, the six checks, snap-to-passing |
| `references/marks-and-anatomy.md` | Mark specs, spacers, labels, figures, hero number |
| `references/interaction.md` | Tooltips & hover, filters & time ranges |
| `references/components.md` | The pieces a chart is made of - build each in plain HTML |
| `references/anti-patterns.md` | **What goes wrong - check every chart against this** |
| `references/palette.md` | **The reference palette instance** - every parameter, filled in; swap for your brand's |
| `scripts/validate_palette.js` | Runnable six-checks validator (run it; don't eyeball) |

"""Strata-plan number -> registration year calibration from NSW cadastre createdate.
createdate = date the lot entered the digital cadastre. For plans registered before the DCDB went live, that is a
bulk digitisation date (many identical dates in 1992-1993), NOT the registration date. We exclude:
  (a) any createdate shared by >= 5 SP plans (bulk loads), and (b) createdate before 1994-01-01.
Then: Spearman(plannumber, createdate), isotonic fit year ~ plannumber, implied year for SP 10k/50k/80k/100k.
Outputs: public-data/_derived/sp_plans.csv, sp_year_calibration.json, sp_year_calibration.png
"""
import json
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt  # noqa: E402
import numpy as np  # noqa: E402
import pandas as pd  # noqa: E402
from scipy.stats import spearmanr  # noqa: E402
from sklearn.isotonic import IsotonicRegression  # noqa: E402

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
OUT = ROOT / "_derived"

fc = json.load(open(ROOT / "cadastre" / "sp_lots_bbox.geojson", encoding="utf-8"))["features"]
rows = []
for f in fc:
    p, g = f["properties"], f["geometry"]
    ring = g["coordinates"][0] if g["type"] == "Polygon" else g["coordinates"][0][0]
    xs, ys = np.array(ring).T[:2]
    rows.append(dict(plannumber=p["plannumber"], planlabel=p["planlabel"], createdate=p["createdate"],
                     startdate=p["startdate"], lon=xs.mean(), lat=ys.mean(), n_vertices=len(ring)))
sp = pd.DataFrame(rows)
for c in ("createdate", "startdate"):
    sp[c] = pd.to_datetime(sp[c], unit="ms")
# planar area (m2) via simple equirectangular approx at -33.9
sp["area_m2_approx"] = np.nan
for i, f in enumerate(fc):
    g = f["geometry"]
    polys = [g["coordinates"]] if g["type"] == "Polygon" else g["coordinates"]
    a = 0.0
    for poly in polys:
        x, y = np.array(poly[0]).T[:2]
        x = x * 111320 * np.cos(np.radians(-33.9))
        y = y * 110574
        a += 0.5 * abs(np.dot(x, np.roll(y, 1)) - np.dot(y, np.roll(x, 1)))
    sp.loc[i, "area_m2_approx"] = a
sp = sp.groupby("plannumber", as_index=False).agg(createdate=("createdate", "min"), startdate=("startdate", "min"),
                                                  lon=("lon", "mean"), lat=("lat", "mean"),
                                                  area_m2_approx=("area_m2_approx", "sum"), n_polys=("planlabel", "size"))
dup = sp.createdate.map(sp.createdate.value_counts())
sp["bulk_date"] = (dup >= 5) | (sp.createdate < "1994-01-01")
sp["createdate_iso"] = sp.createdate.dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
sp.to_csv(OUT / "sp_plans.csv", index=False)

ok = sp[~sp.bulk_date].copy()
ok["year"] = ok.createdate.dt.year + (ok.createdate.dt.day_of_year - 1) / 365.25
rho, pval = spearmanr(ok.plannumber, ok.year)
iso = IsotonicRegression(out_of_bounds="nan").fit(ok.plannumber, ok.year)
resid = ok.year - iso.predict(ok.plannumber)
# share of plans that are "out of order" by > 1 year vs the isotonic fit
out_of_order = float((resid.abs() > 1).mean())
lin = np.polyfit(ok.plannumber, ok.year, 1)
targets = [10_000, 50_000, 80_000, 100_000]
implied = {}
for t in targets:
    v = float(iso.predict([t])[0])
    near = ok[(ok.plannumber - t).abs() <= 1500]
    implied[t] = dict(isotonic_year=None if np.isnan(v) else round(v, 2),
                      median_year_within_1500=None if near.empty else round(float(near.year.median()), 2),
                      n_within_1500=int(len(near)))
res = dict(n_sp_plans=int(len(sp)), n_bulk_or_pre1994_excluded=int(sp.bulk_date.sum()), n_used=int(len(ok)),
           spearman_rho=round(float(rho), 4), spearman_p=float(pval), share_resid_gt_1yr_vs_isotonic=round(out_of_order, 3),
           median_abs_resid_years=round(float(resid.abs().median()), 3),
           plannumber_range_used=[int(ok.plannumber.min()), int(ok.plannumber.max())],
           linear_fit_year_per_10k_plans=round(lin[0] * 1e4, 3), implied=implied,
           createdate_year_counts_all=sp.createdate.dt.year.value_counts().sort_index().to_dict())
json.dump(res, open(OUT / "sp_year_calibration.json", "w"), indent=1, default=str)
print(json.dumps({k: v for k, v in res.items() if k != "createdate_year_counts_all"}, indent=1, default=str))

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 5), dpi=130)
bulk = sp[sp.bulk_date]
ax.scatter(bulk.plannumber, bulk.createdate.dt.year + bulk.createdate.dt.day_of_year / 365.25, s=8, c="#B4B4B4",
           alpha=0.6, linewidths=0, label=f"excluded: bulk / pre-1994 dates (n={len(bulk)})")
ax.scatter(ok.plannumber, ok.year, s=8, c="#2A6FDB", alpha=0.6, linewidths=0, label=f"used (n={len(ok)})")
xs = np.linspace(ok.plannumber.min(), ok.plannumber.max(), 400)
ax.plot(xs, iso.predict(xs), c="#1B1B1B", lw=2, label="isotonic fit")
ax.set_xlabel("Strata plan number (SP)")
ax.set_ylabel("Cadastre createdate (year)")
ax.set_title(f"SP number vs cadastre createdate, Sydney bbox (Spearman {rho:.3f})", fontsize=11, loc="left")
ax.grid(alpha=0.25, lw=0.5)
for s in ("top", "right"):
    ax.spines[s].set_visible(False)
ax.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=8, loc="upper left")
fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig(OUT / "sp_year_calibration.png")
print("saved plot")
